scenarios.hypothesis: The app recognizes a current owned session and rejects a private request without one.
scenarios.expectedEvidence: The synthetic owner reaches the workspace through the normal session reader. An anonymous browser is redirected to sign in.

scenarios.hypothesis: An authenticated owner cannot gain access to another company's private records by changing identifiers.
scenarios.expectedEvidence: Two synthetic tenants have persisted records. An owner cannot load the other tenant's project details or fetch its authenticated PDF.

scenarios.hypothesis: The owner can create, read, update and delete a client through the workspace.
scenarios.expectedEvidence: Browser interactions produce the expected tenant-scoped database state, including loss of access after deletion.

scenarios.hypothesis: The owner can edit an unaccepted estimate and recover its saved document content and totals.
scenarios.expectedEvidence: An edit survives a reload and renders in the public document with its original total. Chromium also exercises the paginated and full-width editor controls.

scenarios.hypothesis: An anonymous visitor with a valid estimate link sees the public document, and an invalid link fails safely.
scenarios.expectedEvidence: The anonymous document shows the seeded scope, line and total. Invalid-link handling produces the expected denial or not-found state.

scenarios.hypothesis: A recipient can sign the public estimate and recover the signed PDF.
scenarios.expectedEvidence: The app persists the signature and accepted state, and the PDF contains the agreed document data and signature evidence.

scenarios.hypothesis: An audio capture can progress through the actual app, API and Inngest handlers to a persisted estimate draft.
scenarios.expectedEvidence: Synthetic media enters the app and the draft renders in the workspace. Provider transports are simulated. The test makes no live AI or physical-device claim.

scenarios.hypothesis: The desktop description field prevents edits until its client handlers mount. A single replacement after mounting must persist exactly.
scenarios.expectedEvidence: The server-rendered field is disabled or read-only while client scripts are held. After mounting, native input events show the previous value fully selected and the exact replacement is saved in the database.

scenarios.hypothesis: An owner can create a manual project, rename it and permanently delete it from the Projects list.
scenarios.expectedEvidence: New Xtimate creates a new project and blank estimate. The title survives reload. The action removes exactly the new project and its estimate and preserves the fixture's original project.

scenarios.hypothesis: An owner can change the company display name and mailing address through the company settings form.
scenarios.expectedEvidence: The synthetic company row stores the new name, street, city, state and ZIP. A fresh page reload shows those values.

scenarios.hypothesis: An owner can create, edit, organize and delete a fixed-price service and its own Price Book category.
scenarios.expectedEvidence: The new service and category persist with updated names, price and assignment and survive reload. Removing the service and empty category removes their database rows and restores the empty state.

capabilities.reason: Real Google Identity consent, callback, new-account onboarding and recovery need dedicated test-account evidence. The owned session fixture starts after identity verification.
Delivery and callback evidence is missing for email, SMS and WhatsApp in approved provider test environments. Outbound delivery is disabled in the initial campaign.
A Stripe sandbox payment, signed webhook, reconciliation and refund need end-to-end evidence. Seeded invoice presentation cannot establish payment processing.
Approved live-provider runs for transcription and estimate generation need quality, timeout and failure-handling evidence. Local capture coverage uses simulated providers.
Real iOS Safari and Android Chrome still need microphone, camera, permission and interrupted upload evidence. Browser profiles exercise emulated devices.
The campaign has no accessibility gate spanning automation, keyboard and screen-reader checks for the critical journeys.
The QA tenant fixture has no platform privileges. Administrative roles, audit records and support operations need isolated browser evidence.
The campaign needs seller creation, customer approval and updated contract/PDF evidence in the required browser projects.
A release candidate needs a smoke result from the actual release deployment and read-only public checks. Local Supabase runs establish development behavior.
